newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks seen cutting long-term prime next week.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks seen cutting long-term prime next week.

text.p: Japan's three long-term credit banks are likely to cut their long-term prime and debenture coupon rates in a monthly revision early next week, bank sources said on Wednesday.
The prime rate, at which the banks lend to their best customers, has been set at 3.3 percent since June.

The size of the cut has not been decided but a cut of 0.3 percentage point is possible considering the current market environment, they said. But another source hinted at the possibility of a cut of 0.4 point.

The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) is likely to announce its revision on Monday. The other two, the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Nippon Credit Bank (NCB), are expected to follow suit on Tuesday.
The IBJ customarily set its long-term prime rate 0.9 percent point above that of its debenture coupon rate. The other two banks adopt the same prime rate.
The latest IBJ debentures with a 2.4 percent coupon, issued in August, was offered on Wednesday at a yield of around 2.11 percent, traders said.
